facts.raw_span: skin fragility since early infancy
Symptoms improved in winter and worsened in summer
Mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions
Erythematous residual macules from previous erosions
Some lesions had unusual linear geographic contour
Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction
No history of blistering
Serological markers for celiac disease were negative
Complete separation of the stratum corneum
Clean split just above the stratum granulosum
2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene
Normal results for: Collagen IV and VII, α6 and β4 integrines, Laminine-332

concepts.why: The patient's skin fragility since early infancy, superficial skin erosions, and complete separation of the stratum corneum are characteristic of peeling skin syndrome, which is further supported by the genetic study revealing 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene.
The patient's symptoms improving in winter and worsening in summer, along with mild xerosis and superficial skin erosions, are consistent with keratolytic winter erythema.

The patient's superficial skin erosions, erythematous residual macules, and complete separation of the stratum corneum could be indicative of Netherton syndrome, although the normal results for collagen IV and VII, α6 and β4 integrines, and laminine-332 make this diagnosis less likely.

The negative serological markers for celiac disease and normal immunofluorescence mapping results for collagen IV and VII, α6 and β4 integrines, and laminine-332 explain the skin fragility and erosions without indicating an autoimmune or collagen-related disorder.

rationales.F11: Mutations in the CDSN gene are associated with peeling skin syndrome.
